 ## Motivation
 
-EOAs can use [EIP-7702](./eip-7702.md) as a bridge to post-quantum authorization. After migration, the account's non-empty code no longer matches the EIP-7702 delegation format `0xef0100 || delegate_address`, so [EIP-3607](./eip-3607.md) disables its ECDSA transaction authority at the protocol level. However, `ecRecover` ignores account state. A quantum-capable attacker deriving the old ECDSA private key could still authorize token transfers through immutable contracts, including ERC-20 `permit` implementations ([ERC-2612](./eip-2612.md)). This EIP applies the same rule to `ecRecover`: recovery returns zero when the account has non-empty raw code that is not a valid EIP-7702 delegation indicator. This prevents the old ECDSA private key from remaining usable through immutable contracts after the account has migrated to post-quantum authorization.
